<details>
The PKGBUILD contains only standard variable assignments and source array definitions in its global scope. There are no command substitutions, function calls, or executable statements outside of the `package()` function that would be triggered during sourcing. The `source`, `source_x86_64`, and `source_aarch64` arrays reference URLs from the project's official GitHub repository and release pages, which is expected for binary packages. All checksums are provided and not set to 'SKIP', further indicating a trustworthy packaging practice. </details>

<details>
The PKGBUILD fetches prebuilt binaries and a systemd service file from the official GitHub repository of the project, using versioned release URLs. No scripts are executed during build or install, and there is no obfuscated code, network activity at runtime, or unexpected system modifications. <security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The `.SRCINFO` file defines metadata for the `rynas-agent-bin` package and lists sources from the official GitHub repository of the project (https://github.com/rylos/rynas). All source URLs point to versioned, immutable release assets (e.g., `v0.5.0` tag) and are accompanied by valid SHA-256 checksums. The service file is also fetched from the same trusted upstream repository at a specific commit reference via the tag, ensuring reproducibility and integrity.

There are no signs of obfuscated URLs, suspicious scripts, or network requests to third-party or unrelated domains. The package follows standard AUR packaging practices: it provides a binary (`-bin` suffix), targets multiple architectures with appropriate sources, and declares dependencies and optional tools relevant to its functionality (backup and restore operations). No executable logic or build instructions are present in this file—only declarative source and metadata entries.

The use of GitHub Releases for distributing prebuilt binaries is common for `-bin` packages, and the presence of checksums for each binary and auxiliary file further strengthens trust in the sources. While the checksums are not 'SKIP', they are explicitly provided and verifiable. No evidence of tampering, backdoors, or supply chain attacks is present.
</details>
<evidence>
